questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mauritius?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mauritius article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Mauritius?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Mauritius on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mauritius article.

questions.proof: It was formerly ruled by the European countries: France, Portugal, and the United Kingdom, but is now independent from these all European Colonies.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Mauritius?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Location” part of the Mauritius article.

questions.proof: Mauritius is part of the Mascarene Islands along with the French island of Réunion 200 km (124 mi) to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Dutch were the ones who named the island in honor of Prince Maurits van _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Maurits”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mauritius article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The Dutch were the ones who named the island in honor of Prince Maurits van NASSAU.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is about 900 km (559 mi) east of _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “east”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mauritius article, under the heading “Location”.

questions.proof: It is about 900 km (559 mi) east of Madagascar.
